extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, regulated entities, and members of the public (e.g., SSA staff; food and drug manufacturers; HUD stakeholders; BLM and ITC stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply regulatory, organizational, labeling, procedural, and information‑collection criteria stated in Federal Register notices across multiple agencies (SSA organizational statements; FDA temporary permits and CPGs; HUD information collection and program reform notices; BLM NEPA/right‑of‑way considerations; ITC procedural determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection submission content requirements (Paperwork Reduction Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice lists the following information: (1) The title of the information collection proposal; (2) the office of the agency to collect the information; (3) the description of the need for the information and its proposed use; (4) the agency form number, if applicable; (5) what members of the public will be affected by the proposal; (6) how frequently information submissions will be required; (7) an estimate of the total numbers of hours needed to prepare the information submission including number of respondents, frequency of response, and hours of response; (8) whether the proposal is new or an extension, reinstatement, or revision of an information collection requirement; and (9) the names and telephone numbers of an agency official familiar with the proposal and of the OMB Desk Officer for the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments referring to the proposal by name and send to the OMB Desk Officer; authority: Section 3507 of the Paperwork Reduction Act, 44 U.S.C. 3507; include estimates of respondents/frequency/hours and contact names/numbers. Copies of proposed forms and supporting documents should be made available by the agency official named in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and labeling requirements for FDA temporary permit market testing (example: 'light eggnog')
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary permit authorized market test of product deviating from U.S. standard of identity for eggnog (deviations: fat content reduced from 8% to 3%; sufficient vitamin A palmitate added so a 4‑fl‑oz serving contains 6% of the U.S. RDA for vitamin A). Permit effective for 15 months beginning on the date the food is introduced into interstate commerce (but not later than specified date). Permit covers specified quantity (84,000 quarts), specified manufacturing site, and specified distribution areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the permited product: the name for the purpose of the permit is 'light eggnog'; the principal display panel must include the statements 'reduced calories' and 'reduced fat' following the name; label must bear comparative statements (e.g., '50 percent less fat than regular eggnog') and comply with reduced calorie labeling requirements in 21 CFR 105.66(d). Reduced fat labeling is acceptable when there is at least a 50% reduction in fat content. The information panel must bear nutrition labeling in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9, and each ingredient must be stated as required by applicable sections of 21 CFR Part 101. The permit limits volumes, manufacturing site, and distribution geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredient and nutrition labeling requirements for FDA market testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the ingredients used in the food must be stated on the label as required by applicable sections of 21 CFR Part 101; nutrition labeling must follow 21 CFR 101.9; reduced calorie labeling must follow 21 CFR 105.66(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative and reduced‑fat/ reduced‑calorie claims must meet the cited CFR thresholds (e.g., at least 50% reduction for reduced fat claim under FDA's current views). Labels must include required statements on principal display and information panel per the permit conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification criteria for products used for odor control in animals (CPG 7125.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Products intended for systemic use in animals to prevent body odors or conception are drugs within the meaning of 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(C) and, absent GRAS evidence from adequate and well‑controlled investigations, are new animal drugs under section 201(w). Topically applied products that contain ingredients with known drug properties (e.g., antibiotics) may be new animal drugs when indicated for control of odor or conception. Topically applied chlorophyll‑based products intended merely to mask or control odors are animal cosmetics (grooming aids) not regulated under the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CPG expands scope to any active ingredient (chlorophyll, antibiotics, other drugs) and establishes regulatory priorities; absence of published literature proving GRAS/effectiveness means product will be treated as a new animal drug requiring approval. Labeling and claims that imply systemic drug action change regulatory status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider before issuing right‑of‑way decisions and need for plan amendment (BLM/ECTC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to issuing decisions regarding an application for a right‑of‑way, BLM will consider public input, environmental impacts, and other factors. If the applicable BLM land use plan does not provide for issuance of the requested right‑of‑way, a plan amendment is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) under NEPA is used to provide the required analysis to amend BLM's planning documents; public contact information and affected counties/land use plans should be cited in the Federal Register notice to inform the public and collect input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired qualities and constraints for proposed changes to Title I program (HUD request for comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD requests public comments and suggestions for possible changes that would make the Title I program more readily available to qualified lenders nationally while preserving the program's actuarial soundness and avoiding pitfalls and problems of third‑party involvement in loan origination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may propose legislative, regulatory, or administrative changes. Desired outcomes include increasing lender participation, reducing program complexity that discourages lenders, maintaining actuarial soundness, and minimizing fraud or program abuses. Written comments must be submitted by a specified due date to the named contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: ODCO (Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Operations) — mission (S2.00)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Operations directs and manages central office and geographically dispersed operations installations; oversees regional operating programs and program management activities; oversees planning and implementation of studies and actions to improve operational effectiveness and efficiency; directs systems and operational integration and strategic planning processes; implements comprehensive systems configuration management, data base management and data administration program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ODCO initiates software and hardware acquisition for SSA and oversees acquisition procedures, policies and activities; directs development of operational and programmatic specifications for new/modified systems and oversees development, validation and implementation phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: ODCO — organization (S2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: ODCO organizational components include: The Deputy Commissioner, Operations (S2); The Assistant Deputy Commissioner, Operations (S2); The Office of Regional Operations (S2D); The Office of Central Processing (S2E); The Office of Systems Support (S2G); The Immediate Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Operations (S2A), which includes the Office of Planning and Operations Management (S2A‑1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Systems Support (S2G) is responsible for requirements development, design, development, testing and validation for programmatic software, software maintenance, comprehensive systems integration and strategic planning, software configuration management, database management, software acquisition procedures, policies and activities; provides administrative support to systems support components.

rubrics_metrics.name: ODCO — functions (S2.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A. The Deputy Commissioner, Operations is directly responsible to the Commissioner for carrying out ODCO’s mission and providing general supervision to ODCO components. B. The Assistant Deputy Commissioner assists and performs duties as prescribed. C. The Office of Regional Operations manages and directs nationwide regional/field/teleservice/processing center networks responsible for RSDI, Black Lung Benefit, and SSI programs. D. The Office of Central Processing manages and directs central office processing components and SSA's computer and telecommunications installations. E/F. Immediate office provides staff assistance including budget review, ADP plan approval, strategic plan oversight, security policies, operating policy development, operations analysis, procurement plan review, and management analysis oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions emphasize management, supervision, planning, procurement oversight, systems and telecommunications coordination, and provision of administrative and technical policy guidance to component offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Regional Operations (ORO) — mission (S2D.00)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Regional Operations is responsible for managing and directing a nationwide network of ROs, FOs, TSCs and PCs responsible for the RSDI programs, the Black Lung Benefits program and the SSI program; provides direct service to the public and processes complex programmatic workloads; directs operational analysis and management support activity that evaluates and develops measures to ensure regional processes meet SSA program and administrative objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORO's mission includes ensuring effective regional processes, operational analysis, and management support to achieve program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORO — organization (S2D.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Associate Deputy Commissioner, Regional Operations, ORO includes: A. The Associate Deputy Commissioner, Regional Operations (S2D); B. The Assistant to the Associate Deputy Commissioner (S2D); C. The Immediate Office of the Associate Deputy Commissioner (S2D); D. The Office of Regional Operations Support (S2DC); E. The Office of the Regional Commissioner (S2D1‑S2DX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational structure identifies lines of supervision and the support office responsible for liaison and operational/management analysis across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORO — functions and delegated responsibilities (S2D.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A. The Associate Deputy Commissioner is responsible to the Deputy Commissioner, Operations for carrying out ORO’s mission and supervises ORO components. B. The Assistant assists the Associate Deputy Commissioner. C. The Immediate Office provides staff assistance on full range of responsibilities. D. The Office of Regional Operations Support advises the Associate Deputy Commissioner, ensures liaison between headquarters and regional operations, addresses regional concerns on legislation/policy/systems, coordinates identification and installation of systems applications, develops security audit trail requirements, analyzes impact of automation, develops staffing and ADP hardware needs, manages implementation of office automation projects and provides input on capacity planning and systems performance. E. The Office of the Regional Commissioner serves as the principal SSA component at the regional level providing program leadership, issuing regional operating policy, directing network of FOs/TSCs/PCs and assuring interaction with HHS ROs and state agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORO Support functions specifically include planning/coordination of operational and management analysis programs, designing studies to measure efficiency/effectiveness, and resolving operating problems. Programmatic coordination with state agencies and external groups is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the Regional Commissioner (ORC) — mission and role (S2D(1‑X).00)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ORC serves as the principal SSA component at the regional level; assures effective SSA interaction with HHS Regional Offices, other Federal agencies, State welfare agencies, State DDSs and other regional/local organizations; provides regional program leadership and technical direction for RSDI, Black Lung and SSI programs; issues regional operating policy and procedures; evaluates program effectiveness; implements national operational/management plans and directs regionwide network of FOs, TSCs and PCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORC manages and coordinates SSA regional operations, provides administrative support, establishes regional priorities and policy directives consistent with national objectives, implements regional public affairs, and oversees coordination with OHA and data operation centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORC — organization (S2D(1‑X).10)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORC organization includes: The Regional Commissioner (S2D1‑S2DX); The Deputy Regional Commissioner (S2D1‑S2DX); The Immediate Office of the Regional Commissioner (S2D1‑S2DX); The Office of the Assistant Regional Commissioner for Program Operations and Systems (S2D1B‑S2DXB); The Office of the Assistant Regional Commissioner for Field Operations (S2D14‑S2DX4); The Office of the Assistant Regional Commissioner for Management and Budget (S2D17‑S2DX7); The Office of the Assistant Regional Commissioner for Processing Center Operations (S2D‑F2,3,4,5,7,9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational delineation defines responsibility for program operations, field consistency, management and budget functions, and processing center oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORC — functions and delegated duties (S2D(1‑X).20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Regional Commissioners manage their regional organizations and carry out the RC mission. B. Deputy Regional Commissioners assist the RC. C. Immediate Office provides high‑level staff assistance and staff support for civil rights/equal opportunity/external affairs. D. Assistant Regional Commissioner for Program Operations and Systems: (1) provides program leadership and issues regional operating policies; (2) assists State DDS agencies in developing and reviewing operating budgets and manages review programs; (3) plans and coordinates regional coverage agreements and negotiations with State/interstate authorities; (4) negotiates and maintains State agreements for SSI supplementation and Medicaid eligibility determinations and monitors State budgets; (5) oversees SSA regional ADP systems and coordinates regional implementation of national systems changes; (6) conducts operational analyses to resolve problems and coordinates with other agencies. E. Assistant Regional Commissioner for Field Operations: (1) provides leadership and guidance to FOs and TSCs; (2) ensures consistency of field operations with policies and is accountable for effectiveness. F. Assistant Regional Commissioner for Management and Budget: (1) furnishes leadership/support in financial/manpower/organizational management; (2) develops regional management policies/procedures consistent with Federal/HHS/SSA requirements; (3) furnishes financial management expertise for State operating budgets; (4) coordinates administrative management issues with HHS RO and headquarters; (5) carries out regional security program. G. Assistant Regional Commissioner for Processing Center Operations: (1) review and authorize or disallow claims for RSI/DI benefits and HI entitlement; (2) determine whether eligibility/payments should be terminated/suspended/continued/adjusted and reconsider determinations; (3) receive, record and deposit SMI premium and overpayment refunds and make representative payee determinations; (4) answer inquiries about individual RSI/DI cases and ensure expeditious processing where hardship indicated; (5) receive and coordinate computer programs and exceptions on case processing, maintain accounting controls and assure by sample audit that magnetic tape records reflect authorized payment actions; (6) coordinate PC operations with other components/agencies as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions include technical direction, issuance of regional operating policy and procedures, budget formulation and monitoring, ADP/systems oversight, intergovernmental agreements, audits and reconciliations, and coordination with Federal agencies such as the Railroad Retirement Board, Veterans' Administration and USPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Regional Operations Support — mission and core duties (S2DC.G0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission items: (1) Advise the Associate Deputy Commissioner, Regional Operations on headquarters support to SSA regional operations components. (2) Ensure effective ongoing liaison between SSA headquarters and the SSA regional operations. (3) Ensure concerns and issues raised by regional operations on proposed legislation, operations policy, procedures and systems matters are addressed by appropriate headquarters components. (4) Coordinate with regional operations management to identify systems needs and manage installation/evaluation of systems applications; develop security audit trail requirements; analyze impact of automation and staffing/ADP hardware needs; manage implementation of office automation projects; provide user input to capacity planning systems and performance issues. (5) Plan and coordinate a continuing program of operational and management analysis throughout regional operations, design and implement studies to measure effectiveness/efficiency of regional processes and identify/resolve operating problems and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Support office is tasked with liaison, systems coordination/requirements, operational analysis, installation oversight, security audit trail requirements, automation impact analyses, and budgeting/planning support for regional operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC procedure for terminating investigations by settlement (Investigation No. 337 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Private parties may file a joint motion to terminate an investigation on the basis of a settlement agreement. The presiding administrative law judge can issue an initial determination terminating the investigation on that basis. The Commission may determine not to review the ALJ's initial determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority for the Commission's determination is section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1337) and § 210.53(h) of the Commission's Interim Rules (19 CFR 210.53(h)). Copies of the non‑confidential version of the ED and other nonconfidential documents are available for inspection during business hours at the Commission; hearing‑impaired persons can contact the Commission's TDD terminal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC authority to vacate temporary orders and release bonds upon settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may vacate temporary limited exclusion orders and temporary cease and desist orders issued in an investigation and release, without forfeiture, bonds posted by parties pursuant to the Commission's determination and orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority for such actions is contained in section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1337). Notices will identify contact counsel for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/format requirement for publishing organizational amendments in Statement of Organization, Functions and Delegations of Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of organizational changes (e.g., abolishment of an office) are published showing the affected Chapter/Part headings (Mission, Organization, Functions) and specifying deleted sections or revised text (example: deletion of 'The Office of Strategic Planning (SAJ)' from SA.10 and SA.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments include effective dates, signature (agency Secretary), FR Doc citation and billing code; revision text or deletion is shown so public and agency staff can update organizational charts and references.
